speechtext: For breeding purposes and only for thoroughbred registered stock. That was done through the mediation of my live stock commissioner.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Would that include shipments for exhibition purposes too ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Would it include sending stock to exhibitions ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
That is another matter. We have also obtained special rates for exhibitions, but what I am speaking of are the ordinary shipments by farmers which are made every day in the year. If a farmer inwestern Ontario wants, to buy a bull for the improvement of stock in Ottawa or in this neighbourhood he can get about half rate on the shipment of that animal if he presents a certificate showing that the animal is thoroughbred. In the same way, if you want to send an animal to the Northwest Territories, or the maritime provinces, or anywhere in Canada, this arrangement is made for the special purpose of encouraging the improvement of stock. We appealed to the railways and after a good deal of negotiation and trouble we got a special rate. I must congratulate the railways upon being sufficiently public-spirited to agree to this arrangement in the interest of live stock men. Difficulties were constantly arising as to what pedigrees should be recognized. There were different kinds of pedigrees and the railway companies frequently made complaint to us, as the department at whose instigation and at whose request this privilege was given, saying that they were troubled and bothered because they got all sorts of pedigrees issued by different associations and they did not know which to recognize. This came to a head last winter when the railway companies threatened that they would have to abrogate the privilege. When it came to that point the question of the nationalization of records was proceeding, and we expressed the hope that in a short time we would be able to issue national records when all other records in Canada would be practically wiped out or ignored. In the process of these negotiations the railways came to the live stock commissioner

and through him to me and they said : We will continue these rates, but we want you to indicate to us which records we are to recognize. My colleague, the hon. Minister of Customs (Mr. Paterson), has also come to me and asked what records he should recognize of animals brought in from abroad for breeding purposes and entitled to free entry, and I have instructed my live stock commissioner to go into the matter to see what report he can make upon it. While the movement for the nationalization of records was in progress the suggestion -was made, either by the railways or the live stock commissioner-I forget which-that we should get up a certain form of record or pedigree, that that should be the recognized form and that the railways, when they get that kind of form, would know at once that it was the recognized pedigree and they must give the better rates. That negotiation is in process to-day and I think it is very well understood that the railways are only going to recognize pedigrees which are stamped by the Department of Agriculture.
But, that point has nothing whatever to do with the transference of the records to Ottawa. It is a matter of general application. It is a matter with which personally I have very little to do except to authorize my live stock commissioner to go ahead. It is a matter in which the live stock commissioner, working in harmony with the officials and the representatives of different breeders' associations, has been negotiating with the rest. That matter as to the transference of the records here has been described a little incorrectly, or, at least, certainly not consistently with my interpretation of what occurred. My hon. friend says from this letter that at the convention that took place a year ago last March in Ottawm the live stock men asked for the nationalization of the records but wanted to keep their records-in their own hands. I said certainly that I would not consent for a moment on behalf of the Department of Agriculture to interfere with the management of the records, but I did point out very clearly to them that to do the work which they asked me to do, namely, to affix the departmental stamp to each pedigree as it was issued, required that an officer of mine should have access to their books, should have an opportunity of looking over and investigating the way in which they were issuing their pedigrees, or else I could not take the responsibility of affixing a government seal to these pedigrees. If I did that without examining into the method pursued it would be a mere perfunctory operation which would be of no value to them, which would do no good and which might discredit the department. If it were to be anything more than a mere perfunctory operation it would require that my officer should see how the certificates were issued by each record association, and that he should satisfy himself that they were carrying on that work not in a way dictated by us but in accordance with their own rules and regulations. That is the whole sum and substance of our supervision.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Then they will have to have an office here and keep the books here ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes. I do not see how that work could be satisfactorily performed unless the issuing of these pedigrees by all these associations is carried on here. That is the wThole sum and substance of the difficulty or difference or grievance. I may say that up to the present time every breeders' association which has been in negotiation with my department has acceded to my request in that respect, with the single exception of the Holstein Breeders' Association.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Is it a matter of compulsion. or is it optional with themselves ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Entirely optional.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They may come around yet ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They may. I wrote to them the other day, impressing upon them that they would stand in the way of their own interests if they held out in this case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What explanation do the Holstein men give ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I have had no explanation, except that they do not wish to move to Ottawa, the present holder of the office preferring to retain it in his own hands.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What is his name ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Mr. Clemons.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Where is the office of the Holstein Breeders' Association at present ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: At St. George, in the county of Brant.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I may say that the people of the west consider that the live stock department in charge of Mr. Hodgson is doing a very valuable work in the way of bringing the western men and the eastern men engaged in stock interests together. That department has done a great deal to advance the interests of the stockmen of the west, especially by securing for us better facilities for shipping stock on the railways. I hope the work will be continued.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I would like the minister to inform the committee whether he will continue to incorporate other associations, or w'hether the policy will be limited to those now in existence ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
By the law I can only incorporate one association for each breed. There are some breeds which are not incorporated, but I would be very glad if they could fulfil the conditions to be incorporated, and I have instructed the Live Stock Commissioner to encourage that as much as [DOT]possible. For instance, there is no associa-

tion of the breeders of thoroughbred horses in Canada. Canadian breeders have to register in the United States. I think it would be very desirable, in the interest of horse breeding in Canada, to have such an association, and I would be glad to encourage it in every way. However, it is quite open to the breeders of thoroughbred horses to have such an association or not, just as they choose. There is no coercion on the part of the department, but my policy is to encourage and help it in every way possible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I understood that the Act which was introduced a little while ago was by way of compromise to get over a difficulty and have the various associations concentrated here. Having that in view, I thought probably the policy of the government would be not to establish any more associations, with the object of completely nationalizing this matter in the end, by getting the various associations to surrender their rights and to come under the control of the government. I am not saying that would be the best policy, because I am not sufficiently informed to form an opinion, but I want to know if that was the view of the government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: With regard to getting the associations under the control of the government. my policy is the very opposite. I think it is in the interest of the country that the management of these associations should be in the hands of the breeders and not under the control of the government or of any department. At the same time, I think the department can serve these people in a limited way, and I want to do that. With regard to forming new associations, there can be only one association for each distinct breed or class of animals. Where one is already formed, no other can be formed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What I referred to was the registration being in the hands of the government and other matters being in the hands of the different associations. '

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
The breeders do not think so, and I have not wished in any way to interfere with that feeling on their part. In all my communications with them I have been very careful to insist that the government would take upon itself just as little interference with their work as was possible to carry out their views, and what I am doing is being done only at their request.
I want it thoroughly understood by tbe country that neither I nor any other officer of my department desires or wall be permitted to encroach in any way upon the rights and privileges of the breeders themselves in their own sphere.
'[DOT]Mj\ CHRISTIE. I think what brought up this whole question of nationalizing the records were the difficulties which the breeder's had with the railways, which thev have had tor several years iu connection with the shipping of thoroughbred live stock. The

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: people of the west could get a thoroughbred animal brought to tbe west from any place in the east at half rates. The difficulty arose iu regard to horses. The Clydesdale Association is the recognized association ; but there is another association called the Draught Horse Association, which relates to horses which are not thoroughbred Clyde horses, but which may be part Shire and part Clyde. That association issues pedigrees, aud these horses were coming out to the western country and being sold as thoroughbred horses. The railways got on to this, and notified the .thoroughbred association that the arrangements made with them would be cancelled unless carried out as agreed. That induced the breeders to look into the matter to see what could be done, and the question came up of nationalizing all associations, with headquarters at Ottawa ; aud the breeders of thoroughbred stock are very anxious that this should be carried out. The minister has stated correctly that the management of every different breed is in the hands of the breeders, while the seal of the government is put on the certificate of any association when the government is satisfied that it is a proper one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Is there any standard of what constitutes a thoroughbred animal ? I suppose there is no means in the hands of the government for checking the registration of animals which are not thoroughbred, though they may be known as such in different sections of the country. It seems to me that in order to make the certificate valuable, there ought to be some means of showing that an animal is really a thoroughbred animal of a certain recognized class.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The breeders themselves are very jealous in regard to that; I do not think anybody could be more so. As a safeguard, however, I may say that under our Dominion Act for the incorporation of record associations the rules and bylaws of the association have to be submitted to the Department of Agriculture and approved before the charter is issued. Then the pedigrees have to be issued under these rules and regulations and the chief use of my officer in examining the pedigree before he stamps it with the official seal is to see that it is issued properly, subject to those rules and regulations. We have first of all to acknowledge the correctness and the propriety of these rules and regulations and then all we have to see is that the pedigree is issued under those rules and regulations. If the rules regarding a society did not secure that it should bo a properly bred animal we would not sanction them and would not give a charter of incorporation to that society.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I have had a little experience in bringing stock to the west. Two

or three years ago I purchased a number of heifers in the east at a certain price, getting about two-thirds of a carload of pure bred live stock. Then I filled up the car with high grade heifers, but I found that I could not get the benefit of the special rate for that reason. I do not know whether anything could be done in connection with the railway companies to give a person who wanted to bring out say half a carload of pure bred stock and the balance grades the benefit of the special rate. I figured the matter out from every point, and I found that it was to my advantage to pay the regular shipping rate, the carload rate, and take the full carload.
I only wanted about twenty pure bred, and when I put in the other ten I found it was cheaper for me to pay the regular rate. It is not every farmer who can afford and has the capital to invest in a full carload of pure bred stock and therefore he receives no benefit from the special rate. Some arrangement should be made between the association and the railway companies whereby farmers would be able to get the benefit of the special rates. I was told by the railway companies that if every one of these had been thoroughbred except one I would have to pay the full rate. It would be a good thing for the breeders in the east as well as those in the west if some arrangement could be made whereby we would have a special rate on less than a full carload.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Arrangements have been made for a special rate for the carriage of pure bred stock. Of course if you do not take a carload you cannot get the carload rate. The arrangement most usually practised is for two or three people to combine together and take up a carload, in which case they get not only the benefit of the rates, but also cheaper care. However, I shall bring the matter before my live stock officials and see if some improvement cannot be made.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: It is not easy to go among your neighbours and find out which one wants to get thoroughbred stock. I am speaking of an individual case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What is the scale of rates that the railroad will give under the Dominion Association of record as compared with the rates that are being given already to the individual breeders' association ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There is no difference. Lately we have had just as good rates as we expect to have in the future unless we can make better arrangements.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Then it will not make them any higher ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I hope that perhaps in the future we will be able to get better terms than in the past. What I meant was that
the railways found so much confusion regarding pedigrees that they threatened to take away the advantage.
Cattle quarantine-further amount required, $40,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: How much was the old amount?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: A hundred and fifty, I think.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I wish to ask the minister what course is usually pursued in regard to quarantining cattle?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: That is rather a broad question. Does my hon. friend mean cattle coming into the country?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They are kept for ninety days in quarantine at the quarantine station when coming in from Europe or any port not in America. We have no detention on the American frontier, except that if they do not bring a certificate that there is no disease where they came from with certain exceptions, and if they do not bring a turberculine test certificate we detain them until they are tested. That takes two or three days.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I wish to ask for some information with respect to the spread of glanders among horses. I have a communication here from a gentleman in my own county. I shall not read it all but shall quote a paragraph or two. He says :
About August 1st last I bought a horse from a farmer near here, and about September 30th the government veterinarian called and found the said horse to have symptoms of glanders and ordered same to be destroyed, which was done in his presence, but nothing whatever has been done by way of remuneration for this horse which cost me $65.
Further on he says :
I was put to about $25 expense by being unable to use my stable and by pulling down and rebuilding same. You will kindly take this matter up for me with the proper parties, which I hope will act wisely in the matter.
(Sgd.) J. M. BRUMMELL,
Mona Road.
February 14, 1905.
This seems to he a case of hardship, but it is possible the minister may be able to give the committee a satisfactory explanation. In looking over the report of the Dominion veterinarian, Doctor J. G. Rutherford, I find several references to the question of the spread of glanders among horses. At page 11 of that report the gentleman says :
I regret to have to report that it has been necessary, during the past year^ to deal with a large number of cases of glanders. The disease has, as usual, prevailed to a greater extent in the' Northwest Territories than elsewhere in the Dominion, 219 horses having been destroyed

there during the year. This is a considerable increase over previous years.
The minister will notice that the spread of glanders in the Northwest Territories is on the increase. Further on he says:
The serious outbreak discovered in the Ottawa district in August, 1902, has claimed a great deal of attention, and largely occupied the time of several of our officers.
A number of minor outbreaks have also been dealt with in Ontario and Quebec, while several cases have occurred in British Columbia. The disease made its appearance in the Yukon Territory during the winter months, and a considerable number of horces have been destroyed by the territorial authorities. 313 horses have been killed during the year by our officers, While a very large number of contact animals have been submitted to the mallein test and dealt with on the system outlined in mv report of last year.
Coming to the question of compensation, at the same page, he says :
I would, however, strongly recommend that some compensation should he paid to owners of horses slaughtered after reacting to the third test, so long as they show no clinical symptoms of the disease. While there may be a question as to the necessity, or even the wisdom, of paying compensation for horses killed when clini-oally affected such animals being highly dangerous not only to other horses but also to human beings.
It appears, In the opinion of the chief veterinary, that horses afflicted with glanders are dangerous, not only to other horses with whom they come in contact, but to human beings such as the man engaged in taking care of them and working them. Further on he says :
The experience of ail other countries goes to show that the payment of a reasonable compensation for animals destroyed is one of the strongest inducements to owners to report outbreaks of disease to the proper authorities.
Then he gives the number of horses destroyed by the various veterinary inspectors in different parts of the Dominion. When a veterinary surgeon enters a farmer's stable, finds a horse affected with glanders, and decides, after thorough examination, that the animal should be killed and orders it to be killed for the better protection of the other horses in that neighbourhood, it seems to me that the government should make some provision for the payment of at least' some portion of the amount which the farmer has to lose. Take the case of the gentleman I have mentioned, who bought a horse for $65, which the veterinary ordered to be killed. It was killed in his presence, so that the owner lost the $65 and m addition had to pull down and rebuild , stable at a cost of $25. The animal was killed in his own interest to some extent but also, according to the report of the chief veterinary, in the interests of the other owners of horses in that neighbourhood It will be remembered that this man bought the Mr. BL,AIM.
horse from one of his own neighbours, which the veterinary surgeon ordered to be destroyed. I think that the law should be so changed that when an animal of this kind is killed the government should pay him some compensation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I agree with my hon. friend, but the question is one that has come up a good many times in this House, and there has always been very considerable disinclination shown by parliament to the payment of compensation. My hon. friend can well remember the discussions we have had regarding the payment of compensation in the case of animals infected with tuberculosis, which were killed to prevent the spread of the disease, and the same question has arisen on other occasions in connection with other diseases. There have been sporadic cases of glanders throughout the country, but more largely in the Northwest than in the east, and the department did not see its way clear to grant compensation, in the face of the views expressed in parliament. No doubt there were some individual cases of hardship. In fact some came before me that concerning which I felt the greatest hesitancy, but at the same time I did not see how I could give compensation without being properly authorized. The disease, however, seemed to be spreading, and it was represented to me that it was because no compensation was being paid. On this account the owners of animals afflicted with the disease were keeping them concealed and using them and spreading the disease, whereas if compensation were allowed they would perhaps have drawn the attention of the veterinaries to the cases and have been willing to have the animals slaughtered. After discussing the matter very carefully with my colleagues last summer and also iu consequence partly of certain discussions here when we amended the Contagious Diseases of Animals' Act, I eventually recommended the passing of an order which would authorize me to pay compensation where the animals were clinically affected. An animal is clinically affected when the disease is apparent to the ordinary uneducated eye. The owner could see that the animal was diseased without knowing what the disease was. Under such circumstances we felt that the animal had reached the stage when it was practically worthless and therefore we need not pay any compensation. However, we passed the order on the 19th September last, authorizing me to pay compensation when the animals were not clinically affected but reacted to the mallein test, which is supposed to be an absolute proof of the presence of glanders. M,v veterinary said that the danger of spreading the disease was not so great in the case of animals clinically affected as in the case of animals which had come in contact with those and

had become merely affected by the disease but did not show it, but in which the disease was liable at any moment to show. The result was that when an animal was found to have come in contact with one clinically affected, we tested it with the mallein test. But first of all wre made regulations by which, at the option of the owner, he might have the animal quarantined. Otherwise it would be slaughtered and no compensation given.
This went on some little time, and we found a great deal of feeling throughout the country. Some people got compensation and their neighbours did not. It was difficult to. explain the difference between one case and another. The ordinary person who did not receive the explanation could not understand the difference and many felt they were being badly treated. This occasioned a great deal of difficulty. And we found again that people who had clinically affected horses were using them as much as they could, but trying to conceal the symptoms, and probably spreading the disease. Many representations were made to me by members of parliament and others throughout the country ; and, eventually, after careful consideration, it was decided to undertake a vigorous campaign against the disease and stamp it out as far as possible. For this purpose, we decided to pay compensation in every case and to slaughter all horses affected, wherever found, without reference to the desire of the owner. On that understanding a further Order in Council was passed on the 25th of March last, authorizing me to slaughter horses affected with glanders and to pay the compensation which the law provides in other similar cases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What would that be ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Two-thirds of the value of the animal as estimated by the veterinary surgeon who authorizes the slaughter. This is the same as in the case of other animals slaughtered under similar circumstances. I find that, since this Order in Council was passed and with the activity with which I considered it necessary to prosecute this campaign to stamp out this disease, we are killing a great many horses and paying out a very large amount of money. I shall be obliged to ask parliament, for the next year, to give me a very considerably larger sum to deal with this disease in this way.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: How much has been paid out since this order came into force in March last ?	,

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Since the commencement of payment, the sum paid out is $29,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Mostly in what part of the Dominion ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Wherever a ease has occurred.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Where has the disease been most prevalent ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: In the Northwest. At present there are two or three outbreaks in Quebec that have been occasioning a good deal of trouble. But the Northwest appears to be the chief seat of the disease. It is about a year or a year and a half ago that we first found cases in Quebec. There have been a good many about Ottawa. Last summer or fall, about 75 or 80 horses were slaughtered within five miles of where we sit.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Can that be ' traced to the importation of western or Mexican horses ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: No, I do not think so. That statement has been made, and it may be correct ; but we have no proof, and I think we would have had proof if it had been true.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: This is going to run into a large sum of money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes. I have told my colleagues that I would probably have to ask for $100,000 additional.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Has the hon. minister paid out any sums for horses in the Northwest ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, I think so. We have been dealing with every part of the country exactly the same.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: A great many horses were killed by order of the veterinary of the Mounted Police at Fort Saskatchewan.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: When ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Last November and December.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: If they were not clinically affected we would pay compensation for them. I have already explained that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Some complained that the veterinary had ordered horses to be killed that need not have been killed. I refer to the country east and north of Bteaver lake.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I can look up that instance. We have constantly had representations of that kind, and I have had them carefully looked into. I have been disposed to deal with such cases on the principle of giving the owner the benefit of the doubt, because I have felt that often it was a case of hardship. Still, I never had authority to pay compensation for the slaughter of horses for glanders until September 19th last. Miany cases occurred before that-scattered cases. There were many cases of hardship in the Northwest in the case of settlers whom I would have been glad to deal with generously had I had authority to do anything, but I could

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Does the kon. minister include Manitoba when he speaks of the ' Northwest.'
work. I will deal with Manitoba just as I have dealt with every other province, but I cannot undertake to pay compensation for horses, the order for slaughter of which was issued by the provincial government

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: How long is it since compensation was paid in Manitoba ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: None was paid until September 19.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Have they been receiving compensation there since September 19?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Any horses that were slaughtered by any of my officers since the 19th of September last were compensated for provided they were clinically affected. This was up to March 25, when the Order in Council was passed to allow me to pay for any horse slaughtered on account of glanders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I have had a good deal to do with this question of glanders in Manitoba since I came here, because in my own district the people have sustained great losses. I have taken up this question with the chief veterinary officer, but he has only been allowing compensation in Manitoba since January last. I understand that compensation was not given until some arrangement was made between this government and the government of Manitoba. I think it would be only fair in Manitoba to those who have sustained losses through this- cause that the rule should be made retroactive so as to place the people of Manitoba on the same level as the people of other provinces. During the months of December and January, I believe, about twenty-five horses were slaughtered in my own district for which no compensation was given. Those in other provinces who had sustained similar losses having been compensated, I feel that we are entitled to the same treatment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
My hon. friend (Mr. Staples) is not fully seized of the facts. The orders for the slaughter of the horses to which he has referred were issued by the provincial government of Manitoba, and with that work 1 had nothing to do. While we were at work in this matter the provincial government also entered upon the work. The provincial government asked my department to take over the business of settling for horses killed on this account in Manitoba. I agreed to do this, but. at the same time. I said I could not be responsible for what the provincial officers had been doing, that I could only act through my own officers. The arrangement was concluded about January between the chief veterinary officer of the department and the provincial authorities. Since that time, I understand, the provincial govern-Mr. FISHER.
and carried out by the provincial officers. We only pay compensation under any circumstances, for any animals in any part of the country, the slaughter of which has been ordered by my own officers.
Mr. STAPLE'S. The provincial authorities, I understand, have turned the whole matter over now to the Dominion authorities, but when this matter was under the jurisdiction of the provincial government, and when those who had their horses slaughtered asked for compensation, the answer they invariably got was : We have nothing to do with it, it is under the jurisdiction of the federal government. Now, the provincial government, las I -understand, were getting ready to hand over the ''entire jurisdiction to this 'government, the department here were willing to take it over. Now, as this transfer was contemplated ever since September, I think that those parties in the province of Manitoba who have had to lose their horses should receive compensation up to that date. I know farmers out there who had to slaughter their last horse, and they can ill afford to suffer the loss. There Is another question. I would ask that the government here appoint local veter-inaries as well as district veterinaries, I understand tnat the officers now looking after glanders in Manitoba are appointing certain veterinaries whose jurisdiction covers large districts. The local council asked that you should appoint as well a local veterinary in each municipality, and let them report to those who have jurisdiction over a larger district. I think the minister will see the force of that. A disease breaks out, aud by the time you reach the man who has to issue a certificate, and before the horse can be slaughtered, the disease may have spread. There is another difficulty. According to the Act a person is noit entitled to compensation unless the horse reacts to the third test. The trouble is that the moment the farmer-I won't say all the farmers, but a certain class of horse dealers-the moment they see a horse has the sign of glanders, they immediately trade him off. I believe that if fair compensation was granted for a horse that showed the slightest sign of the disease, we would much sooner stamp the disease out than we can do when we have to wait until the horse reacts to the third test.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
My hon. friend (Mr. Staples), not unnaturally, confuses these different orders. When we dealt with the question of the mallein test, we gave a certain option to the owner, that if he was not satisfied with the first test he might hold

his horse In quarantine, in which case he could not sell it except under severe penalty, and the purchaser could get hack at him without any trouble. He could hold the horse in quarantine and afterwards have it re-tested. This was an option which we gave to the owner, because sometimes he was not satisfied with the first test. But it is only when the owner desires to do so, and if the owner so desires and takes that option, we also say that we do not then undertake to pay compensation. If he is going to get his compensation he must hold to the first test. If he is not satisfied to do that, he can hold his horse in quarantine, and if it is retested and found to be diseased, he will have to lose his chance for compensation. We do that for the purpose of discouraging the holding of an animal in quarantine which we believe is diseased. I may say ithat the mallein test is looked upon by veterinaries as a pretty fair test, and we believe that a horse which has re-acted to the mallein test is diseased and ought to be slaughtered. If a man insists upon holding his horse after it has re-acted on that test, we think he ought to lose his chance of getting compensation. If he were to sell it in the way my hon. friend points out, he would be subject to a severe penalty under the law, and the purchaser would be easily able to get back his purchase money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I am glad to hear the Minister of Agriculture say that he has decided to grant compensation in all cases in which horses are slaughtered with the intention of trying to stamp out this disease of glanders. Only the other day, in one of the smaller newspapers of the Northwest, I saw a statement to the effect that the department had decided to grant this compensation in cases where there were clinical symptoms. It is a question in which I have been taking some interest, and I was surprised to find that it was not made more generally known that the department had changed its policy in this respect. There is another question that I would like to bring up in connection with this change of policy on the part of the department. On the 19th of September last, apparently, the minister was first authorized to grant compensation for horses which showed no clinical symptoms, hut which re-acted to the mallein test. Between that time and the 25th of March, when the new policy was adopted, there have been a considerable number of horses slaughtered. It is not always quite certain, even when the symptoms appear to be clear to the veterinary who happens to be examining, that a horse is affected with glanders. Veterinaries are liable to err just as much as doctors. I am convinced in my experience -with outbreaks of glanders in the Northwest that many mistakes have been made, that horses have been condemned as having clinical symptoms and have been slaughtered by the government officers 213

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.

speechtext: which have not been affected by glanders at all. Now, It is probable there were many such cases between the 19th of September and the 25th of March, and I think it would be good policy in consideration of any cases of hardship which may have occurred during that period to make this order retro-ative, at any rate, as far back as the 19th of September last. I think no harm will be done by doing so. I further think that information in regard to the new policy of the department should be spread broadcast through the country. A great effort ought to be made to stamp out this disease. I think when it is known that the government will pay compensation, even when there are clinical symptoms present, it will encourage the owners of horses to bring out any horse which is under suspicion and have it examined. In this way the department will be more likely to stamp out the disease.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: It _ would be difficult to make this retroactive. I am afraid if we once began that we would never know where to stop. I would not like to start it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Suppose I were able to testify from personal knowledge of cases where men had lost their horses slaughtered, and suppose that what I said was corroborated by other strong evidence, in that case I think compensation should be allowed. I might ask the hon. minister why it was that the province of Manitoba was not considered until some time in January, when other provinces were receiving compensation ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: It was due to some objections, the Manitoba government themselves had to handing over the work to us. We had been negotiating for some time and we were ready to do it, but they did not seem to want us to take it over.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Did not the Order in Council apply to all Canada 1
Mr. FISHER, Yes. It was not undertaken in Manitoba because the local government officers were doing the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Why had you not the same right to go into Manitoba and deal with the disease there as you had in other provinces?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Because the local government was doing the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
They were doing the work because it was very necessary that they should do it until it was taken over. I do not see any reason why the province of Manitoba should be held up when all the other provinces in Canada were being assisted.
Mr. FISHER, They were not held up in the slightest degree.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They did not receive the same assistance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: That was their own fault.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Will the hon. minister consider the advisability of appointing a local veterinary surgeon ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: We tried that but we found that it does not work well at all. The local veterinary is frequently influenced by the feeling in the neighbourhood and we have to send a man from some other place. It is the duty of any local veterinary, whether called in or not, if he knows of a case, to report it immediately to the department. We have found that the handling of these cases, especially where compensation is concerned, by a local veterinary is very unsatisfactory and I could not undertake to return to that method.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Are the horses to be killed under the instructions of one veterinary examiner and as the result of one examination, or under the instructions of the government veterinary examiner without any eorrobor-rative evidence ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, they are to be killed on the report of the government verterinary. That is the case in regard to the slaughter of other animals-hogs, cattle and horses.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I rather agree with my hon. friend from Qu'Appelle (Mr. Lake) that the hon. minister should have made this Order in Council a little better known to the people of Canada, and I think, that, particularly when the House is in session, these special orders which are passed by the government should be made known to the House at least. Here is a special Order in Council passed on the 20th March when this House was in session by the instruction of the hon. Minister of Agriculture himself ; yet, the House has been in session continuously since January 11 to this moment and the hon. minister has never thought it to be his duty to make a statement to that effect in the House so that the members would know it. When Orders in Council are passed regarding important questions touching the whole of the people of Canada I think the hon. minister should make a statement to that effect, so that members of parliament should be well informed on these questions. My hon. friend shakes his head.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I only shake my head because that is not the practice.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I am condemning the method because it is not the practice. Here is the hon. Minister of Agriculture, having charge of the duty of checking the spread of a very dangerous disease among horses, a certain Order in Council is adopted and then cancelled and a very important Order in Council is passed on the 19th of September, a few days before the issue of the writs for the general election. It may have some significance perhaps, but I will not discuss that, nor another Order in Council passed on Mr. STAPLES.
March 20th. I am very much surprised that the hon. minister did not think it his duty to stand up and make a statement so that those representing different districts throughout Canada interested in this question would have an opportunity of communicating the contents of this Order in Council to their constituents instead of having to wait for several weeks for the people to be informed on the question. I condemn legislation by Order in Council.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: In reference to the question of whether this provision should be retroactive or not I wish to point out that it appears that a man whose horse was examined on the 25th March by the veterinary inspector, and found to have clinical symptoms, will receive compensation for the horse. If the veterinary happened to get round to his neighbour the day before, that neighbour would receive no compensation for his horse. It seems a case of hardship and there will be a great deal of heart burning in certain places in regard to this matter. As the department have practically agreed that this compensation should be granted for all horses slaughtered they should have gone one step farther and made the 19th September the date from which the payment of compensation should begin.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: If the committee will pardon me a moment or two there is a question that is raised here which is I think a somewhat Important one. Is this legislating by Order in Council for the payment of public money without the authorization of parliament ? If you can do this it seems to me you can do almost anything.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There must be an appropriation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There must be an appropriation, but there must be an appropriation for an expenditure in view of that legislation by Order in Council. No such policy as this has been pursued in Canada before. The Minister of Agriculture is launching out under an Order in Council which includes a ciass of expenditure which has not before been recognized by parliament but which is distinctly outside of the policy heretofore in vogue. For instance, there was no authority at all at a certain time to pay even part of the value of any horses which were killed on account of this disease. I think that policy remained up to or within a very short time ago-up to September, do I understand the minister ? Am I right in this that up to September there was no payment for horses that became diseased in this way and were slaughtered by the orders of the veterinary ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There was no provision by Order in Council, but the statute always has contemplated that provision being made by Order in Council at any time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: My hon. friend to a certain extent, perhaps, is right, but still not quite. There is a large vote every year for the protecting the health of animals and for cattle quarantine. That money is first of all voted by the House and it is then expended under the Animals Contagious Diseases Act, which Act authorizes the payment of compensation under Order in Council. The power was fully in existence when the vote was passed. It has been exercised in days gone by in regard to other diseases, and power was clearly and distinctly given by the Act to Council to pass an order at any time in regard to this class of payments.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I think it is stretching it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: To-day, for instance, there is $10,000 additional on this year, which is very largely due. Of course, if the House says that it will not grant the money, the Order in Council will have to be rescinded.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
That same argument could be used in every case. I think it would be better to ask the House for the money first. My hon. friend talks about $100,000. If he makes a policy of this kind general throughout the Dominion, $100,000 would be a small amount compared with what he would have to pay. It would amount to hundreds of thousands. Then the point comes, how far should the government, acting for every individual in the country, bear the whole or the major part of the expense? Then, the minister will have to be very careful of two things: first, what diseases come over the border, and, secondly, what steps are taken in our own country to stamp out these diseases? A very profitable trade could be carried on in old and diseased 2131
horses if the government paid two-thirds of the cost in every case. In the third place, he will have to be careful about the veterinarians he appoints, on whose recommendations the money is paid. I quite agree with the minister that local veterinarians should not be relied on in every case. Not that they will not be found honest, but the pressure upon them is often too great to withstand.
At six o'clock, committee took recess.
