maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I was going to ask the minister at six o'clock if this compensation allowed for animals slaughtered to prevent the spread of contagious diseases applies to anything except horses with glanders ?
Mr. FISHER, It does not apply to horses with any other disease. We pay compensation as a regular rule for hogs that are slaughtered for cholera. We also paid for many years for cattle affected with the Pictou cattle disease, a disease prevalent in a very small area of Nova Scotia and in Prince Edward Island. By the law the minister can pay compensation, but as a matter of practice the minister has never done so except on Order in Council. Council passes regulations authorizing such payments and the regulations do not authorize any payment of compensation except for hogs slaughtered for cholera, cattle affected with the Pictou, cattle disease and for horses affected with glanders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The reason I asked the question is that in the locality where I live a very serious disease has broken out among horses this last year. Is the minister aware of the fact ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The maladie du colt.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I think we have authority to pay compensation for horses affected with maladie du colt. I must have It looked up but I think that is the case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: That I believe is a more serious and fatal disease than glanders at the present moment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: It is very serious.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
And if it spreads to any extent I am certain it will be more serious. At present it prevails in a portion of Alberta, but we have had some hundreds of horses affected there in the last few years. I know one herd in particular where 20 mares and an entire horse worth about $1,000 have been under quarantine for 12 months before I left home. The owner has been ordered to slaughter the horses, but the animals are still alive. I think the government are experimenting to some extent with the disease at a large quarantine station at

Lethbridge. X would like to know the results.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
My hon. friend is quite correct in what he says about this disease. It was introduced from the United States some little time ago. It was only recently,
I think perhaps 15 or 16 months ago, that the chief veterinarian adviser of the department found some cases of it. Knowing the very serious character of the disease immediate active steps were taken to examine into the condition of affairs and as my hon. friend says it was found that there was a considerable number of affected animals. To act promptly we wished to see at first whether there was any necessity for slaughter, and we therefore cellected all the animals we could find affected with the disease in a certain quarantine station. My chief veterinary inspector went up and consulted with the horse owners and ranchers in the neighbourhood and some considerable number-speaking from memory I think over 200 horses- were collected in the quarantine grounds to which my hon. friend refers. We have been watching it there. The disease is chiefly visible at certain times in the year ; in the spring it is more likely to be found than at any other time. iMy hon. friend probably is aware of the nature of the disease. The chief veterinary officer, Dr. Rutherford, is at present up in the Northwest examining further into the condition of affairs. He has been up there now two or three weeks and is going to stay there two or three weeks more for the express purpose of investigating the condition of affairs. We have not slaughtered animals for the disease yet wherever we find them ; we quarantine them and if we slaughter them we will probably have to pay compensation according to the advice I receive from the chief veterinary officer. Here is a regulation relating to it:
Every owner, breeder or importer of, or dealer in horses, shall on perceiving the appearance of maladie du coit, among the animals owned by him or under his special care, give immediate notice to the Minister of Agriculture and to the nearest veterinary inspector of the Department of Agriculture of the facts discovered by him as aforesaid.
Then it goes on about the entire horses and the rules against their running at large.
No animal which is affected with maladie du coit shall be permitted to run at large or to come in contact with any animal which is not so affected.
And the officers were authorized to quarantine places where these horses had been, and they have power to isolate and quarantine these animals.
The veterinaiy director general may, from time to time, order the slaughter, castration or other disposition of animals affected with mala-die du coit.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: We have not yet taken power to pay compensation. I believe that when my veterinary adviser returns, if the report is such as to require any slaughter of these animals we will be obliged to pay compensation. The law requires two-thirds of the value of the animal to be paid up to a certain sum. I hope within a few weeks to' get a very complete report on the present condition of affairs, and until that comes I would not like to say anything more definite at the present time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Can the minister say where the disease came from ? Is it supposed to have originated somewhere in Montana or Wyoming ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There is a certain section of the United States where this disease has been common for a good many years. It was restricted in the United States by severe precautions and the authorities there asserted and our reports from there indicated that it was very circumscribed. Just where the disease came from into Canada we do not know. It had evidently been in the country for some little time before any report was made too late probably to make any satisfactory statement as to where it came from. I have no doubt it came across the line but just where I cannot say.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: How any veterinary surgeon inspectors are there in Manitoba, who are they and where are they located ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I am speaking rather from memory. There are Dr. Little, of Winnipeg, and Dr. McGillivray, also of Winnipeg, Dr. McGillivray, I think, did not reside in Winnipeg. I think he went there to live after he had been appointed one of our officers. Dr. Torrance is another. Then there is Dr. Robertson, who is at Emmerson, I think, and there is Dr. Schultz, of Gladstone.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Has each doctor a district?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Each has authority anywhere in the province, but each probably does his main work in some district. Those in Winnipeg are liable to be called out of the city from any part of the province.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Upon what date did the minister take over the control of matters with regard to glanders in Manitoba?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: nor did they, that both authorities should engage in it. But, when we made changes affecting the w'hole Dominion including Manitoba, it was suggested that we should take over the whole matter and that the Manitoba government should cease to deal with it. Eventually we came to an arrangement of that kind.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Then, I am to understand that, owing to the minister not exercising the authority he has, and the fact of the provincial government dealing with the glanders question, those who were unfortunate enough to have horses slaughtered on this account will receive no compensation. In view of the fact that people suffering similar losses elsewhere were compensated, I think that is hardly fair. I would like an explanation from the minister why Manitoba is not dealt with the same as other provinces from September, when the Order in Council was passed up to the time when this department took control of them.
Mr. FISHER, Of course, the work done by that provincial government was done under the provincial laws. I am not familiar with these laws, but I am informed that there was a provision by which certain of the municipalities could enforce the law.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: But the provincial law could not prohibit the Minister of Agriculture from exercising his authority under the Dominion law?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Then, I claim that the rule should be made retroactive and that these people should be compensated.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: That is a matter that may be open to argument.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I was glad to hear the minister speak of maladie du colt and to know that he has recognized the importance of this matter. It is a far more fatal disease than glanders, and the shipping of a carload of horses from where it exists may spread it all over Canada, for it is a hard disease to check. If there is danger of it being brought in from the United States the horses coming from that country should be examined with the greatest care. I would urge the minister to guard carefully against the spread of the disease where it exists.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
The minister has referred to the provincial law giving the municipalities jurisdiction in regard to glanders. I think this was optional. Some of the municipalities gave compensation and some did not. I read in one of our local papers that one of the Dominion officials, Doctor Schultz has been in my district and, in conjunction with the local veterinary, has ordered the shooting of a number of horses for glanders. That particular municipality
gave compensation. But I see that they have had a great deal of glanders in a district probably forty miles in length and that many horses had to be destroyed. The municipality has suffered so much that they have given notice of the repeal of the by-law for it was too great a drain on the municipal treasury. I presume that the horses shot now will be compensated for by the Dominion government. Do the officials to which the minister has referred make reports at stated intervals to the department, or do they report to the head office in Winnipeg? Is there any superior in Winnipeg to whom they report?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Every case is reported here direct-a separate report for each case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Doctor Little, Doctor McGillivray and Doctor Torrance are all in Winnipeg. Are all on an equality, or is there any to whom the others report ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: All report here direct. Speaking from memory-as the chief veterinary officer is in the west, and I have nobody at hand who can give me the exact information-I think that one of these officers was given some general charge of the whole province. But they all have authority in all parts of the province and they all report here and not to any officer in Manitoba. But one of them is looked upon as the leader.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Doctor McGillivray ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, I think so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What salaries do these officers receive?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I cannot say offhand, but I think they receive from SI,200 to $1,500 a year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: On what principle are these officers appointed ? Why are they all selected from Winnipeg ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They are not. Dr. McGillivray did not live in AVinnipeg until he was appointed. Dr. Schultz did not live in Winnipeg. There Is another of these officers living in Crystal City. I think that Dr. Little and Dr. Torrance were the only two who lived in Winnipeg until Dr. McGillivray moved there. And I think the reason Dr. McGiMivray moved to Winnipeg is that as the railways centre in there one can more quickly and cheaply reach any part of the province from Winnipeg than from any other place.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Other veterinaries made application for appointment. For instance, take the southwestern part of Manitoba. There was one veterinary in Carman, a thoroughly eligible man, from a political as well as from every other standpoint. And Carman is a central point. Yet this gentleman did not get the appointment. Upon

what principle Is the selection of those officers made ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: My chief veterinary officer is a Manitoba man, and I referred the matter largely to his opinion, as he knows about it more than I do or anybody else, having lived in that province many years and having been a member of the local legislature there, where he had a great deal to do with the framing of the Manitoba law with regard to veterinary work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Does the $1,500 include travelling expenses ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: No ; they send in their expenses.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: It would be satisfactory to the committee if the bon. minister would explain bow be finds that lie has the power to appropriate the money be did last year for the purpose of compensating for the destruction of cattle. At the time that we granted the appropriation last year there was no law in force enabling him to grant compensation to any one in the case of the destruction of cattle on account of glanders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, there was.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: There was a law enabling us to make compensation, but no provision for compensation until an Order in Council was passed. At the time we were making the grant there was no Older in Council. Consequently there was nothing at that time before the House which would authorize the paying of this money. It was oniy subsequently, on the 29th of 'September last, that the Order in Council came into force.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Under the 12th section of the Aot the Governor in Council may order compensation to be paid the owners of animals and also make regulations. Those regulations are embodied in an Order in Council, and then we pass an individual Order in Council for every individual payment.
Mr. R, L. BORDEN. Does the minister, in fixing the compensation, observe the limit set forth in section 12 of the Act of 1903 ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Always.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: This afternoon he said that the limit was two-thirds the value of the animal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, up to a certain point.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The minister did not say that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I think I did.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: He simply said that the amount paid was two-thirds the value of the animal. Will he explain now what it was he did say ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I followed the regulations exactly. There was an Act passed last year changing the compensation from one-third in some cases and three-quarters in others Mr. STAPLES.
to a flat third all through. The statute of 1903 covers the whole Act. Then last session we passed an amendment with regard to compensation alone.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Can the minister tell what amount of money was paid in compensation between the passing of the Order on the 19th of September, to the final order that was passed on the 20th of March ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I cannot say exactly,, because the statement is not divided according to those dates, but from October 22, which was the date of the first payment under the Order in Council of September,, to February 20, there was $8,942 paid. I could not say how much was paid in each province ; but in round figures it was chiefly in the Northwest Territories and: Quebec. There was not one case in the maritime provinces.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Perhaps the minister might give us the figures.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Up to the present date, $29,000 ; up to the 20th of February about $9,000, that was about a month before the change. That is as far as I can give the figures.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: How do the returns look for the present month ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They are pretty heavy. Since this decision to pay for all cases was come to, on an understanding that a most determined effort was to be made to stamp out the disease, I have given orders to my officers to he more active in the matter. I think that within the last month they must have reports coming in for close on to $20,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Is there any prospect of overcoming the disease ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I could not say that yet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Is the payment of this large amount of money liable to be attended with any abuses in the way of claims ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I think not. I have been trying to guard against that. I do not know whether my hon. friend was in when I said that we only ordered the slaughter on the report of our permanent officers, and it is on their valuation of the animal that we pay, we do not allow outside valuation. That is the case with ail the animals slaughtered for which we give compensation. The veterinary who orders the slaughter fixes the value. Then the Act limits the amount of value which may be put upon an animal, so much for a thoroughbred, and less for a grade animal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: What is the average price paid for horses, on a two-thirds valuation ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I am told the payment lately has come to nearly $100 a piece.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: That is a big price for a western horse. Could the hon. gentleman tell us what class of horse it is, is it an ordinary western horse that seems to be affected, or is it the progeny of horses that have been taken from the east ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The horses that come into contact most frequently are the working horses, and in many cases these teams are worth a great deal more than we are allowed to pay compensation for. The horses that are running free we have not got at yet, to any extent.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
You may have a great big proposition.
Mr. FISHER, It is a serious proposition, I grant.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
There is a possibility, it seems to me, that the minister may have to pay in cases that he does not contemplate. The Order in Council referred to, or a summary of it, provides, as the minister says, for compensation in the cases dealt with by subsection 2 of section 12 of the Animals Contagious Diseases Act, of 1903, as amended by chapter 6 of the statutes of 1904. Section 12 of Act of 1903 says :
The Governor in Council may order a compensation to be paid to owners of animals slaughtered under the provisions of this Act.
Of course the general provisions of this Act in that regard would be the preceding section 11 :
The minister may, from time to time, cause to be slaughtered animals suffering from infectious or contagious diseases, or suspected of being affected, and animals which are or have been infected by or in close proximity to a diseased animal or animals suspected of being affected by a contagious disease.
But if the minister will look at section 10, he will find that where the animal is offered for sale it may be seized by any inspector, and so on, who should report the seizure to the mayor, or reeve, or any justice of the peace having jurisdiction, and such mayor, reeve or justice of the peace may call in a veterinary to examine the animal. That is a summary of the clause. Of course it provides that the animal may be destroyed by the officer appointed by the minister, but it also provides that the animal may be destroyed on the order of the mayor, reeve or justice of the peace, on an examination which need not necessarily even be an examination made by one of the veterinaries appointed by the minister. I think that is pretty clear. I am not saying it is a very material point, but it does away with, or brakes in upon what the minister contemplates, that is, that he shall have through his officers complete control of the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Section 12 gives the Governor in Council latitude of paying compensation or not, just as they liae.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Certainly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The Order in Council only authorizes the payment of compensation when the slaughter has been ordered by an officer of the department ; consequently, I think that fear which the hon. gentleman has expressed in regard to the latitude allowed under section 10 would hardly come in.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The hon. minister might possibly be able to carry it out in that way. It says' that the inspectors are authorized to slaughter, and then it says that the minister is authorized to order compensation to be *paid to the owners of animals which are slaughtered under the provisions of section 12 and the amendments thereto. Section 12 provides for compensation where an animal is slaughtered under the provisions of this Act. Section 10 provides for the slaughter of an animal in a way which is not contemplated by the Minister, and I am very far from saying that it would be just to deprive a person of compensation because his animal happened to be slaughtered by order of a justice of the peace or mayor or some one of that kind upon an inspection by a local officer when this provision is made in the Act. I think it embraces a larger class of cases than that which he has referred to.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I only referred to that to show that there is no danger.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I hardly think it is a danger. I think it is right enough, but it extends farther than the hon. minister would have us understand.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I would like to ask the hon. minister if the veterinary surgeons who are employed in Manitoba at salaries amounting to $1,500 and expenses are employed the year round working exclusively for'the government, or are they carrying on their own business and doing what the government require of them ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: They are supposed to give all their time to our work and they are employed the year round.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Does that apply to the veterinaries in the Territories ?
Mr. FISHER, In the Territories the work is done almost exclusively by officers of the mounted police, who work under my department in that respect. They are employed in their work as members of the mounted police and we make them a special allowance for the work they do for the Agricultural Department. But, I have some special officers in the Northwest and what I have stated applies to these. I would like to say that there is an officer in Winnipeg, Dr. Torrence, who is not paid by the year but who is paid

so much a day when he is employed. He does not give his whole time to our work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Would the hon. minister say who these officers report to and from whom they get their instructions ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The chief veterinary officer, Dr. Rutherford.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Has the hon. minister gentlemen employed in Ontario in the same way ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I see that we have here in Ottawa, G. W. Higginson. Is he in connection with the department ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Yes, he is paid. He is an officer giving his whole time to our work. I think that Dr. Higginson lives at Rockland. He is doing certain work there in that neighbourhood for us.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Then there is Mr. A. E. Moore.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Dr. Moore is a permanent officer who makes his headquarters here, hut who travels all over the provinces of Ontario and Quebec. He is one of our most valuable officers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Whyte ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: He makes his headquarters tit Sherbrooke, Quebec, and works all along the frontier between Quebec and the United States in connection with the health of animals as well as travelling through the English speaking parts of Quebec.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I see in the Auditor General's Report the name of M. Philps, Chatham. He draws a salary of $50 ; his livery expenses amount to $48.50 ; pair of rubber boots $6 and travelling expenses $15.05. What does Mr. Philps do ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: He has been working in connection with the outbreaks of hog cholera. He requires rubber boots to go into the hogpens. We have to provide all our officers with rubber boots. They put on these boots to go into the hog pens and when they come out they take them off and wash them thoroughly so as not to carry infection. If they went into the hog-pens with leather boots the infection would be carried by them.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: He gets a salary of $50 and his livery bill is $48 ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: Quite -possibly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: May I ask the hon. minister what information he has from Essex and Kent relative to the hog plague ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: My information is that it is lessening to some extent. I cannot speak more positively than that. This spring we have not had so many reports and we have not had so many deaths as we had last year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: May I ask the hon. minister if the officials who have been employed for the last four or five years are lessening in number ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I do not think I have taken off any of the officers yet. I hardly think the situation would justify me in doing so, but just as soon as it will justify it there will be a decrease.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: While I am thoroughly acquainted with the regulations regarding the hog plague there I may say that complaint is made that hogs are allowed to be taken from one township in which they have the disease and in which a quarantine has been ordered by a veterinary surgeon into another township where there is no disease perhaps ten miles distant. Is that a fact ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: No, that is not a fact unless the hogs are being taken to a packing house. We allow hogs to be shipped from a township which is quarantined because of the presence of disease to a packing house when they are fit for slaughter. Of course, this refers to animals that are free from disease. We do not allow them to be shipped to any other place, but we have a special provision allowing hogs to be shipped to a packing house on condition that they are immediately slaughtered. We had a good deal of difficulty in regard to that because people sold hogs which were not ready for slaughter and upon arriving at the slaughter house, finding that they were not fit for slaughter, they were resold to farmers in the neighbourhood. We traced innumerable outbreaks of hog cholera to that cause. We made a regulation providing that the hogs were to be immediately slaughtered and the packing house people were strictly enjoined against shipping them out or selling them alive. Since the enforcement of this restriction the number of outbreaks of hog cholera has materially decreased in the neighbourhood of slaughter houses.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: The disease has abated in my district to such an extent that we think the number of veterinary surgeons now employed to inspect these hogs is unnecessary. Instead of being veterinary surgeons they are hog inspectors who are employed to inspect the class of hogs that the hon. minister has spoken of and which are being sent to these factories. If a heavy fine were imposed upon these factories receiving these hogs for re-selling them, it would be a great saving to the country and the hon. minister would be able to reduce the number of officers who are drawing large salaries in my district amounting to $1,200 and $1,500 a year and expenses.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
We allow the hogs to be shipped provided they are healthy, and therefore they have to be inspected by some competent person who can say whether
*6713

they are healthy or not. The people there have been very urgent indeed in their request to us that we should give as much latitude as possible for the shipment of hogs. My hon. friend himself, I am sure, has had representations as to the stringency of the quarantine, and we have had similar representations from municipal authorities as well as from individuals. I have done everything I possibly could to make the quarantine as little irksome as possible. For that purpose I have retained inspectors with the view of enabling the people to ship out such hogs as they might, so that their feeding operations should not be interfered with more than was necessary in the public interest. I confess that the work is quite expensive, but it has been done in the interest of the people there, and I think it was justifiable, because those people make their living and derive the profits of their farms largely from the hogs they ship. AA'e have to continue the inspection for some time after the outbreak, because we cannot be sure that the disease will not reappear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I admit that it is a [DOT]difficult question, and the minister has my sympathy to some extent. He knows that my district is probably more heavily affected in this matter than any other in the Dominion. There are a great many complaints there, and I think they are quite justified. Where a farmer had only three or four hogs affected out of 100 or 150, it seemed wholly unnecessary to kill the whole herd. Owing to the way the farmers were treated by the inspectors, they simply evaded the law, and I do not believe there has been one farmer in a hundred in the last year or two who reported the disease to the inspectors at all. I believe there are a number of inspectors there who should be dismissed. These men . feel that they must do something for the money which the government is paying them; but it would be far better for the government to deal with the local inspectors, who, I think are more capable of taking care of the matter than the officials the government has there at present.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I would ask the minister what progress is being made in stamping out sheep scab, which was found to exist three or four months ago in the province of Ontario?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I am afraid I cannot give my hon. friend much information on that subject. The officers of the department have been watching it and following up cases wherever they could find them. I have not heard of any particular report within the last two or three weeks. Before that a considerable number of cases were discovered. Aly hon. friend knows that it is a disease which we do not require to slaughter for. It can be cured by proper
treatment, and we impress that fact on the farmers. AVe have even gone so far as to send inspectors where we have heard of cases, and have given full instructions. AAre of course quarantine the affected flocks and have them thoroughly disinfected and cleaned. I think we have located every case; I do not think there is any case that we have not dealt with. In the spring, when the farmers shear their sheep, they are pretty sure to notice any symptoms of the disease, and every case that is discovered is treated. I do not think there is a flock infected in Ontario to-day which has not been attended to. More than that I cannot say.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: AAThat does the department term the hog disease that exists in my riding?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: AA'e generally call it hog cholera.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Our veterinaries state that it is not hog cholera, but a certain plague. I may say that there are scores of farmers whose hogs have had this disease, but they have not reported it, and in a great many cases their hogs have got well. They have simply killed two or three which were sick, out of the flock, and the rest have got well. I think it is entirely unnecessary to kill the number of hogs which the officials of the department have demanded to be killed in the past.
Air. MAiCLAREN. In what section of Ontario does this sheep disease exist ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I do not think I ought to say that, because I should have to speak entirely from memory, and I might make a mistake.
Air. AVILLIAM AA'RIGHT. I would like to call the attention of the members of this House to the over lapping of authority between the Dominion government and the local governments in regard not only to diseases of animals, but to various agricultural matters. AVe have local government officials as well as Dominion officials dealing with the matters which we have been discussing tonight. That seems to be an unnecessary overlapping of duties, and some arrangement should be made to have the authority vested exclusively either in the Dominion or in the provinces. There may be good reasons why this work can be handled better by the Dominion government, but they have not become manifest to me yet from the discussion that has taken place or from anything that I have been able to read on the question. I think these matters could be better handled by the local governments, which already incur very large expenditures for these purposes. I think we ought to look into this question and see whether a reduction of the expense could not be made, either by a joint arrangement be-

tween the Minister of Agriculture of the Dominion and the Ministers of Agriculture of the various provinces, or by transferring the whole business to the Dominion or to the provinces. The position seems to be this, that any province that takes hold of this matter energetically, and stamps out disease in the province would only have for its pains the privilege of putting up its share of the expense, while other provinces would throw the responsibility entirely on the Dominion ; thus a premium would be put on the carelessness of those provinces. But if the Dominion undertakes the responsibility, it should handle the business exclusively. I would like to ask the minister whether any steps have been taken with a view to coming to an arrangement with the various provinces with regard to matters touching agriculture in general.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
Of course, there is no line or organization which can prevent the passage of contagious diseases from one province to another. If one province is neglectful of these matters the other provinces will suffer. The constitution seems to allow provinces to pass laws relating to the health of animals, and also enjoins on the Dominion parliament to do this, too. We have passed certain laws. Those laws the provincial governments may enforce or not, just as they like. The provincial governments have power to pass laws also. In Ontario, for instance, there is quite a strong law [DOT]against glanders, but at the same time the provincial government have taken no active steps to enforce that law. Some years ago they did for a number of years, but they have not done anything recently, and one of the most expensive enforcements of that law was here in Ottawa, where we had, a year and a-half ago, to slaughter a large number of horses in this neighbourhood. The provincial government knew perfectly well that the disease was in existence. We [DOT]had another reason why it was difficult for a provincial government to do this. Some cases of the disease spread across the bridges here into Quebec, and we traced cases of glanders across the river and up into the lumber camps which had come straight from Ottawa, and the people there complained that this disease came straight from the province of Ontario. It was a matter which was not provincial, but interprovincial, and it seems that, under such circumstances, the provinces have a rather fair claim that the Dominion government should deal with these things. I confess that since I have been in office dealing with these things the work has grown a good deal. We have demands to do things, and, in view of the interests involved, I have tried to meet the demands as much as possible. maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
With regard to making the order in March apply to last September, if the minister will look at the Act carefully he will agree that in the amended Act of 1904 coupled with section 12 of the Act of 1903, it is optional with the Governor in Council to give compensation or not, but once compensation is given it can only be given in one way. The government can give compensation or not, but, if it gives compensation, it must give it in accordance Mr. STAPLES.
with the terms of the statute and cannot discriminate as between animals exhibiting a greater or less degree of disease. The minister pointed out-and it is very reasonable-that, in case of clinical sym-toms, the government did not contemplate paying under the Order in Council of last fall. But the Act, after providing that the minister can provide for the slaughter of animals to prevent the spread of contagious diseases, goes on to say :
The Governor in Council may order compensation to be paid to the owners of animals slaughtered under the provisions of this Act.
I need not read subsections 2 and 3, as they are repealed by the Act of 1904, and others substituted. Linder the subsections repealed there is a limit to the compensation to be paid, but under the new provision there is no limit except that it is to be two-thirds of the value of the animal before it became affected with infectious or contagious disease, or it came in contact with or in dangerous proximity to animals affected. Thus it is provided by the statute that the compensation should be a certain thing. I submit to the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Fisher) and also to the Minister of Finance (Mr. Fielding) who has had a very long experience in the construction of statutes, that the government have the alternative of giving compensation or not giving it, but there is no discretion in the Governor in Council in the amount of compensation or the conditions under which it is to be given if any is given. Therefore, I would submit that you cannot legally or fairly discriminate as to cases arising between the Orders in Council of September, 1904, and the Order in Council of 1905. I am glad that it is so, because I believe it will be a good thing if the minister could see his way to remedy what will be to some extent a grievance-that these people in the west by reason of, I will not say the conflict, between the authorities, but of lack of adjustment between them, should fail to receive compensation in any way. I do not ask the minister to decide the matter now, but to look into it carefully. If he will turn to what I understand to be the embodiment of this Order in Council in this blue book and read the express provision there, I think he will be convinced that it is a fair reading of the provision that compensation should be made to these people that had animals slaughtered between September last and March last. I quote from page 173 of the report of the Minister of Agriculture, the latter part of paragraph 9 :
And the Minister of Agriculture is hereby authorized to order compensation to be paid to the owners of such animals at the rate set forth in subsection 2 of section 12 of the Animal Contagious Diseases Act, 1903, as amended by chapter 6 of the statutes of 1904.
That is, compensation should be made, if made at all, to the extent of two-thirds

of the value of the animal without discriminating as to whether the disease is ascertained by examination by the eye or by scientific test.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext: I am ready to look into the matter, because I should be glad if I am allowed to make compensation in any case of hardship.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF MILITIA CAMP AT KENTV1LLE, N.S.
speechtext:
I am glad that the minister (Mr. Fisher) has agreed to look into the subject. The people of Manitoba only ask fair play in this matter. The people of the other provinces have been compensated since September and I do not see any reason why, especially as evidence can be brought to show that these animals were slaughtered on the certificate of a veterinary, the owners should not be compensated just as the owners of animals similarly slaughtered in other provinces have been.
